label: H.R. 5221

summary: H.R. 5221, titled the Preventing Auto Recycling Theft Act or the PART Act, aims to prevent the theft of catalytic converters and other precious metal car parts. It updates vehicle theft prevention standards to include catalytic converters, establishes a grant program for stamping vehicle identification numbers onto catalytic converters, sets record-keeping and payment traceability requirements for businesses handling parts containing precious metals, prohibits the sale of converters with removed or tampered markings, and establishes new federal criminal penalties for catalytic converter theft and trafficking.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to apply for grants to provide public catalytic converter stamping services and equipment.
affected_groups.group: Law enforcement agencies, automobile dealers, vehicle fleet owners, repair shops, and nonprofits

affected_groups.effect: Required to comply with updated regulations to include catalytic converters in vehicle theft prevention standards and ensure proper marking.
Must collect and retain specific seller records and identification information for at least two years.
affected_groups.group: Vehicle salvagers, dismantlers, recyclers, and repair businesses

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from using cash or cryptocurrency for transactions, must use traceable payments, and cannot trade converters with tampered markings.
affected_groups.group: Sellers and buyers of catalytic converters

affected_groups.effect: Subject to federal fines and up to 5 years in prison.
affected_groups.group: Individuals who commit catalytic converter theft or trafficking

key_provisions: Directs the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to revise vehicle theft prevention standards to include catalytic converters and ensure they are marked conspicuously with traceable identification numbers.

Establishes a $7,000,000 grant program within the Department of Transportation to fund equipment and materials for die or pin stamping vehicle identification numbers onto catalytic converters and applying high-heat theft deterrence paint.

Requires businesses engaged in salvaging, dismantling, recycling, or repairing motor vehicles or parts containing precious metals to retain seller records and identification details for at least two years.
Bans the sale or purchase of catalytic converters using cash or cryptocurrency, requiring traceable forms of payment such as checks or wire transfers.
Prohibits selling or purchasing catalytic converters that have had their identifying markings removed or tampered with.
Creates a new federal criminal offense for stealing a catalytic converter or purchasing a stolen one with intent to distribute, carrying penalties of a fine, imprisonment for up to 5 years, or both.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 5221, titled the Preventing Auto Recycling Theft Act or the PART Act, aims to prevent the theft of catalytic converters and other precious metal car parts. It updates vehicle theft prevention standards to include catalytic converters, establishes a grant program for stamping vehicle identification numbers onto catalytic converters, sets record-keeping and payment traceability requirements for businesses handling parts containing precious metals, prohibits the sale of converters with removed or tampered markings, and establishes new federal criminal penalties for catalytic converter theft and trafficking.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a comprehensive federal framework combining manufacturing standards, tracking systems, grant funding for preventative marking, strict business record-keeping, payment restrictions, and federal criminal penalties targeting catalytic converter theft.
